verdicts.why: Fisk already runs his empire in season 1 (he blackmails Osborn in S1 ep 3 and takes his place back from the Hobgoblin in S1 ep 12). He only forms the Insidious Six in S2 ep 1, so Fisk's Empire has to come first. The rest of the record stays as it is.

Lonnie is one of the former WWI soldiers and POWs: Janet finds out in episode 3 that Addison, Lincoln and Marko were prisoners of war, and episodes 5 and 6 tell their war past. The dataset already gives Marko, Leyden and Addison 'U.S. Army' ahead of Silvermane's Mob. The left at Spider-Noir stays.

groups: (Tombstone/the Big Man's organization: name per owner call)

verdicts.why: The past group is on screen in S2 ep 8 (show ep 21): Sable says 'Daddy was so right to fire you', and Hammerhead answers 'That's what I get for taking pity on the boss's daughter'. He then serves the Big Man (the name is still an owner call: the screen only says 'the Big Man's' operation). In ep 23 he turns on Tombstone at the summit ('Hammerhead's the new Big Man'), so add Independent and a left. The proposal had dropped both, even though its own evidence calls for the left.

The show tells it in S2 (the Savage Land arc, 'Reunion'): the Mutates 'whom Magneto created years earlier' now 'serve the Savage Land's new master', and Ka-Zar resents him for meddling. That makes Magneto their former master, just as Sinister is counted, so it is a past stage ahead of the Acolytes. 'The Savage Land Mutates' is already the dataset's name.

In 'Time Fugitives' (S2 ep 7-8) Apocalypse poses as a Friends of Humanity member next to Graydon Creed (Marvel Database: 'Impersonates FOH member'), and undercover service counts. After the X-Men wreck the lab he slips away and goes back to leading his Horsemen.

Killmonger says it on screen in What If...? S1E6: 'I uncovered plans to assassinate Tony Stark while on a deep cover operation inside the Ten Rings.' Undercover service counts, and 'The Ten Rings' is already the dataset's What If name. The left stays.

The past military service is on screen in S2 ep 4: 'Served in the Philippines during the war. Court-martialed, dishonorably discharged for black market profiteering', and Hunt tells of his torture by the Japanese. But the episode never names his branch ('Army' comes only from the MCU Wiki), so use the dataset's generic 'U.S. Military'.
Zuri says on screen that N'Jobu took a War Dog assignment in America, so he served the War Dogs (the dataset's 'The War Dogs', as for Zuri and Nakia) until he betrayed Wakanda. The left stays.

Luke Cage S2 ep 1 names the gang on screen: Bobby Fish says the Rivals were 'Shades, Comanche, and Romeo's old crew', and Shades and Comanche trade the Rivals greeting. It is a past group, keyed to his first title (Luke Cage S1). The Stokes stage stays and there is no left.

After he mutates, Landon is the Kingpin's lieutenant and chief scientist (S3 ep 8, S4 ep 2), and no return to the Brand Corporation is shown. The owner already ruled in morning_calls.json: 'drop the final Brand Corporation stage (no return shown)'.

Mordo comes out of the New York Sanctum as Sorcerer Supreme, and Strange tells him on screen that killing Stephen Strange was 'your ticket to getting the Sanctum, to becoming Sorcerer Supreme, and to joining ... the Illuminati'. So he was in the order of sorcerers first ('Masters of the Mystic Arts', the dataset's name for it) and joined the Illuminati after.

In X-Men '97 S2 Candra belongs to Rama-Tut's court in 3000 B.C. (the dataset files his regime as 'Ancient Egypt'). His regime ends for her when he flees and Apocalypse destroys the city, the same way Rama-Tut's own record ends it (Independent, left at X-Men '97 S2). Add "X-Men '97 S2" to the left list, as the proposal says. Being worshipped as the X-Ternal is not membership.
